Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week — we liked the latency profile for short-chat flows. We're launching two additional internal products in Q1 (agent assistant for support and a summarization pipeline for legal documents). Those are expected to add bursty, high-context requests (avg seq len ~1.2k) and a steady embedding pipeline for search.

We already have a hosted account with you (current monthly ~600M tokens). Before we talk formal expansion I wanted to understand:
- How incremental commits work if we want to add these two workloads (new teams) across the same account
- Whether token-based volume discounts stack across products or are siloed per route
- Any minimum time commitments for the added commit (monthly vs annual) and ramp protections for early months

Can you share a simple example of how you would price an incremental +20% commit for a new team vs a separate new commit for each product? Also any guidance on cache/batching suggestions that would preserve quality while lowering unit cost would be helpful.

Appreciate quick guidance — procurement is on standby.

Best,
Sarah
Head of ML, VoyagerAI

Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the usage context. Quick plenary answer up front: volume discounts are applied at the account level and can be structured either as incremental add-on commits or as a consolidated single commit; the optimal path depends on predictability, desired term, and whether you want separate rollbacks per product.

I'll loop in Aditya for two sample math paths (incremental single-commit vs per-product commits) and Stephanie for a short MAP (mutual action plan) and a pricing spreadsheet we can use to iterate.

Two quick notes while we wait for the detailed math:
- Discounts scale by monthly committed token bands (we show per-token price at commit tiers). You get the higher discount once the commit crosses the next band cumulatively across products.
- For bursty, high-context requests we usually recommend a mix of (a) a lite quantized variant for non-critical assists, (b) prefix caching for repeated prompts, and (c) controlled batching for high throughput jobs — all of which can materially lower unit cost without changing model choices.

Will follow up with concrete examples in the next email.

— Lauren
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Mike — looping in a concise worked example so you can see dollar impact and flexibility. I attached a quick spreadsheet (voyager_pricing_v3.xlsx) with two scenarios: consolidated incremental commit vs per-product commits. High level:

Scenario A — Consolidated incremental commit (single +20% account commit)
- Current baseline: 600M tokens/month at $0.0018/token (example current blended rate)
- +20% incremental commit = +120M tokens/month committed
- New blended band pushes you closer to the next discount (example: that additional 120M moves you from 10% -> 13% discount at current list)
- Effective per-token after discounts + committed credits — scenario shows ~8% unit cost reduction compared to paying that incremental usage as overage on existing plan
- Benefit: single SLA, single billing line, flexible cross-team usage
- Tradeoff: rollback affects entire account (we can do routing policies to isolate usage if needed)

Scenario B — Per-product incremental commits (two separate +10% commits)
- Adds explicit headroom per product and gives you independent rollouts and rollbacks
- Slightly lower aggregate discount in our example because bands are evaluated per commit block; combined discount ends up ~11% vs 13% in Scenario A
- Benefit: operational isolation and clearer chargeback for product teams

Other important mechanics:
- Minimum term: we support monthly or 12-month commits. Annual commits provide the best unit price and come with SLA uplift.
- Ramp protection: for the first 3 months we provide a graded true-up mechanism (you won't be charged the full committed overage if actual is < 50% of committed additional for month 1; the spreadsheet shows the graduated true-up).
- Exchange/rollback: we can convert unused committed tokens into a credit for other Redwood products in the same account subject to a 90-day notice on annuals.

Operational recommendation (for VoyagerAI):
- If you expect the two new products to have correlated peak windows and shared customers, go consolidated (Scenario A) for better pricing and simpler ops.
- If you want strict budget allocation and independent pilots, go per-product commits (Scenario B).

I'll leave the spreadsheet for your team; Lauren / Stephanie will follow up with a short MAP and a suggested DocuSign link for the commitment path you prefer.

Thanks,
Aditya
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
